title: Grateful Dead Live at Hollywood Bowl on 1972-06-17
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/48k) ->Adobe Audition v3 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Shure Unidyne III -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-40)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1972 Hollywood Bowl show with a standout first‑time Stella Blue and clear Keith organ, captured in an excellent front‑row audience tape.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the historic performance – Pigpen’s last appearance on organ, the debut of Stella Blue, and tight playing throughout – while noting the recording is a well‑balanced front‑row audience capture with surprisingly clear organ and Garcia’s guitar. A few reviewers mention minor drop‑outs and pitch quirks that were later fixed, but overall the tape is praised as highly listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈90%) are 4‑5 stars and highlight both strong musical performance and good audio quality; only a handful of zero‑star or critical notes exist, leading to a solid 4.2 rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Front‑row box seat capture gives clear organ and Garcia’s guitar; mic placement makes Pigpen’s organ unusually prominent. Minor dropout in The Other One was spliced, and a few reviewers note slight speed/pitch inconsistencies that have been corrected.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical Europe ’72 set, shortened but well‑paced; warm‑up first set with solid transitions, a concise second set that keeps the momentum without lingering.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is captured directly from his amp, sounding clear and powerful; fans note his humorous “help prevent forest fires” quip.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil opens with a bronchitis joke, provides solid bass throughout, and his spoken bits are heard early in the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s banter about the hat incident and audience interaction is mentioned by several reviewers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s organ work is prominently featured – especially on Stella Blue and other songs – thanks to favorable mic placement; his presence is a highlight of the tape.
